plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 (21-layer three-cavity Ge/ZnS Fabry-Perot filter) based on iteration_10 results showing 0.909 best_target_score with 9 valid candidates. Feedback directives specify: (1) replace uniform-random initialization with resonance-centered sampling at λ/2n for cavities, (2) enforce 500nm hard thickness upper bound, (3) seed 40% of population with λ/4n quarter-wave mirrors. Four complementary routes explore: resonance-seeded gradient optimization, evolutionary optimizer comparison, reduced layer count for manufacturability, and two-cavity simplified topology. All routes preserve the verified Ge/ZnS material pair and CaF2 substrate from route_02.

routes.title: Resonance-Seeded Three-Cavity Filter with 500nm Thickness Cap
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses near theoretical half-wave resonance values (λ/2n) for cavity layers and quarter-wave values (λ/4n) for mirror sections, with a 500nm upper bound, will concentrate the search in physically meaningful interference regimes and improve best_target_score convergence compared to uniform-random initialization in route_02.
routes.design_principle: Fabry-Perot cavity resonance occurs when optical thickness equals half-wavelength multiples. Seeding optimization near these values reduces unphysical search volume and accelerates convergence to high-transmittance solutions.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | CaF2 (21 layers total: 3 cavities with alternating Ge/ZnS mirrors)
design_variables: initialization centered on λ/2n for cavities and λ/4n for mirrors
soft_objectives: maximize transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm passbands
minimize transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm stopbands
improve best_target_score over route_02 baseline of 0.909
manufacturing_considerations: 500nm maximum thickness per layer improves deposition uniformity
Ge/ZnS material pair verified for mid-IR transparency
theory_basis: Fabry-Perot resonance condition: optical thickness = m·λ/2 for constructive interference
Quarter-wave stack theory: alternating λ/4n layers create high-reflectance mirrors
expected_advantages: Reduced risk of unphysical thickness combinations
Better alignment with constructive interference regimes from round 2 onward
known_risks: 500nm cap may restrict optimal solutions if thicker cavities are physically required
Resonance seeding may bias search away from non-obvious optimal configurations
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 21-layer dielectric bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate using Ge (high-index) and ZnS (low-index) materials in a three-cavity Fabry-Perot topology. Initialize cavity layer thicknesses near theoretical half-wave resonance values (λ/2n) at 4.45 μm center wavelength, and mirror section thicknesses near quarter-wave values (λ/4n). Enforce hard thickness bounds of 50-500 nm per layer. Seed 40% of initial population with deterministic λ/4n multiples for mirror sections. Optimize for high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm passbands, low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm stopbands, at normal incidence in air. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with resonance-centered initialization. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Implements feedback directive to replace uniform-random initialization with bounded sampling centered on theoretical half-wave resonance values (λ/2n) for cavity layers, enforce 500nm upper thickness limit, and seed 40% of initial population using deterministic λ/4n multiples for mirror sections. This collapses unphysical search volume compared to route_02's broad initialization.

routes.title: Evolutionary Optimization of Three-Cavity Filter with Resonance Seeding
routes.scientific_hypothesis: An evolutionary optimizer with resonance-centered initialization will explore the thickness parameter space more thoroughly than gradient-based optimization, potentially discovering non-local optima that gradient methods miss while maintaining the 500nm thickness constraint.
routes.design_principle: Evolutionary algorithms maintain population diversity and can escape local optima that trap gradient-based methods, particularly in multi-modal optimization landscapes typical of multi-cavity filter design.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | CaF2 (21 layers total: 3 cavities with alternating Ge/ZnS mirrors)
design_variables: evolutionary population initialization centered on λ/2n resonance values
soft_objectives: maximize transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm passbands
minimize transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm stopbands
achieve best_target_score ≥ 0.90 to match route_02 performance
theory_basis: Evolutionary optimization maintains diversity in multi-modal search spaces
Fabry-Perot cavity resonance theory for initialization
expected_advantages: Better exploration of thickness parameter space
Potential to discover non-obvious high-performing configurations
More robust to local optima than gradient methods
known_risks: May require more evaluation rounds to reach comparable scores
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 21-layer dielectric bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate using Ge (high-index) and ZnS (low-index) materials in a three-cavity Fabry-Perot topology. Initialize all layer thicknesses near theoretical half-wave resonance values (λ/2n) at 4.45 μm center wavelength with 50-500 nm bounds. Use evolutionary optimizer with population size 50, mutation rate 0.1, and crossover rate 0.7. Seed 40% of initial population with deterministic λ/4n quarter-wave values for mirror sections. Optimize for high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm passbands, low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm stopbands, at normal incidence in air. routes.revision_reason: Tests alternative optimization strategy (evolutionary vs gradient) while preserving route_02's 21-layer Ge/ZnS three-cavity topology. Complements route_02_refine_01 by comparing optimizer effectiveness with same resonance-seeded initialization.

routes.title: Reduced Layer Count Three-Cavity Filter for Manufacturability
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing layer count from 21 to 19 layers while maintaining three-cavity topology will preserve most optical performance (best_target_score ≥ 0.88) while improving manufacturability through reduced deposition time and cumulative thickness error.
routes.design_principle: Fewer layers reduce cumulative deposition error and stress, but may reduce stopband rejection. Three-cavity topology with 19 layers should maintain adequate passband shaping while being more manufacturable than 21-layer design.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | CaF2 (19 layers total: 3 cavities with reduced mirror pairs)
soft_objectives: maximize transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm passbands
minimize transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm stopbands
achieve best_target_score within 0.03 of route_02 baseline (≥ 0.88)
manufacturing_considerations: 19 layers reduces deposition time by ~10% compared to 21 layers
Reduced cumulative thickness error from fewer interfaces
theory_basis: Layer count affects bandwidth and stopband rejection per evidence on BPF design
Fewer layers reduce cumulative deposition error and stress
expected_advantages: Improved manufacturability with fewer deposition steps
Lower material cost and deposition time
known_risks: Reduced stopband rejection with fewer mirror pairs
May not achieve route_02's 0.909 score with only 19 layers

Optimize for high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm passbands, low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm stopbands, at normal incidence in air. routes.revision_reason: Tests whether 19-layer topology can achieve comparable performance to route_02's 21-layer design while improving manufacturability. Preserves three-cavity Fabry-Perot principle and resonance-seeded initialization from feedback directives.

routes.title: Two-Cavity Simplified Topology with Resonance Seeding
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A two-cavity Fabry-Perot topology with 17 layers will achieve acceptable dual-band performance (best_target_score ≥ 0.85) while significantly simplifying the design and improving manufacturability compared to three-cavity route_02, though with potentially broader passbands.
routes.design_principle: Two-cavity designs have fewer degrees of freedom but are simpler to fabricate and may provide adequate performance if passband width requirements are flexible. Resonance seeding should help maximize performance within reduced design space.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | CaF2 (17 layers total: 2 cavities with alternating Ge/ZnS mirrors)
soft_objectives: maximize transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm passbands
minimize transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm stopbands
achieve best_target_score ≥ 0.85 as acceptable simplification trade-off
manufacturing_considerations: 17 layers reduces deposition time by ~19% compared to 21 layers
Simplest topology among all routes for highest manufacturability
theory_basis: Fabry-Perot cavity count affects passband shape: more cavities produce squarer passbands
Two-cavity designs trade passband sharpness for manufacturability
known_risks: Broader passbands may reduce gas selectivity
Lower stopband rejection with fewer cavities
